articleTitle: A GaN MMIC Wideband Continuous-Mode Doherty Power Amplifier for 6G FR3 cmWave Applications
abstract: This paper presents a 10−14 GHz Doherty power amplifier (PA) implemented in GaN on SiC MMIC process aimed for future 6G FR3 centimeter-wave (cmWave) applications. We propose the theory and design of the continuous-mode (CM) operations to extend Doherty PA bandwidth. To demonstrate the viability of the concept, a prototype GaN MMIC CM Doherty PA was fabricated and fully characterized. Experimental results exhibit a peak power added efficiency (PAE) of 28% − 38% and back-off PAE of 21% − 31%, respectively, with an output power higher than 34 dBm across the operating frequencies.

articleTitle: A High-Pass Distributed Amplifier Operating from 215GHz – 315GHz in a 35nm InGaAs mHEMT Technology
abstract: In this paper, a high-pass distributed amplifier is presented. The distributed amplifier consists of four parallel gain cells using RF shorted stubs at each gain cell at the gate and drain line connection. This way, the classical low-pass artificial transmission line is transformed into a pseudo high-pass artificial transmission line. Small signal measurements and large signal simulation results are shown. The targeted operation band is the WR3.4-Band (220-330 GHz). A 3dB-bandwidth of up to 100 GHz is measured. A maximum gain of up to 9.4 dB is achieved in small signal measurements. The amplifier is produced in a 35 nm InGaAs mHEMT technology.

articleTitle: Simulation by Harmonic Balance Techniques of Non-Linear Circuits Driven by Random Modulated Signals
abstract: A new method is proposed to perform, by Harmonic Balance (HB) techniques, the simulation of non-linear circuits driven by carrier Random-Modulated (RM) signals. The microwave driving random modulated generator is first transformed in an almost periodic generator with two fundamental frequencies: the carrier frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">car</inf>) and, on the other hand, the modulating frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">modframe</inf>) given by the user-defined length (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">modframe</inf>) of the modulating random bit sequence. This random bit sequence is mapped into a random symbol sequence with a symbol period (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">symb</inf>). The random modulated generator becomes then a Pseudo-Random Modulated (PRM) microwave signal generator. An almost-periodic harmonic balance simulation can be then performed with this driving microwave PRM generator. This paper presents the implementation of the PRM microwave generator in a commercially available circuit simulation software. A software-defined demodulation of the output signal of the DUT, with optimal matched filters to respect the Nyquist criteria, is implemented to extract all the linearity and power metrics performances at design circuit level, in the time and frequency-domains. To check the validity of the PRM-HB simulation, a linear circuit driven by a 16 QAM modulated microwave signal is simulated and the EVM is calculated.

articleTitle: RF-DAC-based PA Pre-Distortion using Expanding Non-Linear RF-DAC Scaling
abstract: We present an RF-DAC-based transmitter that uses an expanding characteristic to linearize the PA. Implemented in 22nm FDSOI CMOS, the transmitter operates with a carrier frequency of 12.5GHz, achieving a sample rate of 7GS/s. Measurements with >3.5GSym/s wideband modulated 64QAM SC and OFDM signals show EVM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RMS</inf> <3.83% and ACPR <−32.4dBc when using the RF-DAC-based predistortion. The 1dB compression point is increased by 4.2dB. For multi-GHz wideband modulated signals, a >0.6 percent unit EVM improvement and a >2.5dB ACPR improvement are observed.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Behavioral Modeling of FETs: Toward the Implementation of Deep Neural Networks through Large Signal Data and EDA Tools
abstract: Nonlinear behavioral Field-Effect Transistor (FET) models often rely on large look-up tables extracted from extensive load-pull characterization. Besides the numerical burden, these models have limited extrapolation capabilities and can hardly be made dependent on the device technology. In this paper, we demonstrate that a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based Deep Neural Network (DNN) is an effective alternative modeling approach. The DNN is trained with the load-pull data within a simulation platform where data exchange between an Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tool (such as PathWave ADS) and a programming platform (such as MATLAB) is exploited. As a test case, the DNN model has been extracted for an S-band MACOM 10W GaN power device, for which the Enhanced Poly-Harmonic Distortion (EPHD) behavioral model is also available in the ADS. The accuracy of DNN model is verified against the EPHD model in terms of output power, gain, efficiency, and dynamic load lines. Compared to other behavioral models, the DNN approach is expected to provide superior extrapolation capability and to be easily reconfigurable to add/combine heterogeneous device data e.g. from advanced characterization, including memory, and physical (TCAD, EM) simulations.

articleTitle: A Stacked MOSFET-Based RF Switch with High DC Voltage Handling Capabilities
abstract: A series switch arrangement constructed from stacked MOS transistors and capable of handling high-voltage DC and RF signals is presented in the paper. The result is achieved by using three switch branches, each comprising a resistive bias network that provides uniform voltage division in the stack at DC and AC. A hardware prototype implemented in a 90nm SOI-CMOS process with 3V transistors demonstrated DC voltage handling of ±14V and RF handling of 16V peak with IIP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> =74dBm at 1GHz, insertion loss and isolation of 0.19dB and 55dB respectively, and 0.1dB insertion loss bandwidth of over 4GHz.

articleTitle: 2DEG Charge Density Calculation for HEMT Physics-Based Compact Models by Newton Method
abstract: This work proposes a physically based, High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT) model by directly implementing the implicit equation of the two dimensional electron gas (2DEG) charge density. To achieve this, four iterations of the Newton-Raphson algorithm, together with an appropriate initial value estimation, are embedded in the core model. This approach is effective for any applied gate voltage, particularly in the subthreshold region, without requiring behavioral manipulation of the model equations, as in conventional core models. The proposed model is continuously differentiable, up to any order, accurately. The proposed charge formulation is compared to the ASM model formulation. To show the capability, the model is implemented in Verilog-A to calculate the charge and then the drain current to compare with measurement data.

articleTitle: Low-Cost 10-Watt CW Power Amplifier for Satellite Communication
abstract: This study introduces a cost-effective power amplifier designed for satellite communication applications. The amplifier employs a low-cost surface-mount packaged transistor, typically reserved for low-duty cycle pulsed test conditions, but uniquely adapted here for continuous wave (CW) operation. To mitigate the risk of thermal overload, the design process prioritized efficiency. This was achieved through the implementation of a harmonic tuning approach, with particular attention given to the real part of the impedances experienced by the transistor. Simulations and empirical measurements confirmed the amplifier’s robust performance, delivering a minimum output power of 40 dBm, a drain efficiency ranging from 32% to 42%, and a power gain of 7 to 10 dB across the full bandwidth of 7.25-7.75 GHz, which is allocated for space-to-earth communication links.

articleTitle: Ka-Band Metal-Insulator-Graphene Diode-based Thin-Film Cascaded Reflective-Type Phase Shifter
abstract: This work presents the design, implementation, and characterisation of a K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>-band thin-film two-stage compact analogue phase-shifter. The design exploits a reflective-type configuration which utilizes four metal-insulator-graphene diodes as reflective loads. The fabricated prototype is realised on a 8.1 µm-thick flexible polyimide (PI) substrate and occupies less than 0.7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of chip area including the contact pads. The assessment of the fabricated circuit reveals an S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> performance better than -13 dB and an S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> measurement of -3.3 dB with a tolerance of ± 0.5 dB across the frequency band of 28 – 36 GHz with a tunable phase difference (∆ϕ) exceeding 70°. The introduced flexible thin-film technology promotes the realisation of flexible cost-effective beam steering for smart surfaces and biomedical applications.

articleTitle: A Low-Power 42 to 67 GHz Variable-Gain LNA in 22FDX® on Standard- and High-Resistivity Substrates with 3.4 dB Noise Figure
abstract: This paper describes the design and implementation of a 42-67 GHz LNA using GlobalFoundries’ 22 nm FD-SOI technology, that was fabricated on standard-resistivity as well as on high-resistivity substrate wafers. On the conventional standard-resistivity substrate, the proposed design achieves 3.8 dB of minimal noise-figure for a peak gain of 21.0 dB at its nominal bias under 13.7 mW of power-consumption. The LNA makes use of the unique back-gate bias node of the 22FDX® technology to offer 10 dB of gain-control over a 2 V bias range at the back-gates, and takes up an area of 0.17 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. On the high-resistivity silicon substrate, improvements of 0.9 dB in gain and 0.4 dB in noise-figure are achieved for this LNA, and these improvements are attributed to the increased quality factors of the integrated spiral inductors present in the design.

articleTitle: An Over 100% Fractional Bandwidth Low Noise Amplifier with Gate-Drain Transformer-Feedback in 90-nm CMOS Process
abstract: This paper presents a broadband low noise amplifier (LNA) operating from 13 to 40 GHz, designed for communication applications using TSMC 90-nm CMOS technology. To extend the bandwidth, the gate-drain transformer-feedback technique is employed at each stage. The proposed LNA achieves high gain and low noise figure simultaneously over a wide frequency range, while maintaining low power consumption. Measurement results demonstrate competitive performance, with a peak gain of 15.6 dB and a noise figure ranging from 2.3 to 4.8 dB across a 4-dB bandwidth spanning fro m 13.3 to 40.3 GHz. The DC power consumption of the design is only 11.7 mW, with an IP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> of -12 dBm and IIP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> of -1.6 dBm at 28 GHz. Furthermore, the figure-of-merit (FoM) of this work is calculated to be 19.9 GHz/mW, showing its competitiveness among published Ku-band to Ka-band wideband LNAs. The entire chip occupies a compact area of 0.43 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, including pads.

articleTitle: Layout-Aware Equivalent Circuit Models for Accurate Deembedding and Simulation of mm-Wave CMOS Device Performance
abstract: New equivalent circuit models with layout dependent parameters have been developed for openM1 and shortM1 pads, and full structure with devices to realize accurate high frequency simulation before and after deembedding. The parasitic resistance, inductance, and capacitance (RLC) originated from the pads, transmission lines (TML), and lossy substrate will lead to a dramatic degradation of the current gain and power gain, and thus abnormally low f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MAX</inf> in nanoscale CMOS devices. A clean deembedding achieved by using openM1 and shortM1 to the bottom metal (M1) can achieve super-300 GHz f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MAX</inf> in multi-finger (MF) nMOSFETs with optimized layout aimed at mm-Wave CMOS circuit design. The developed models can accurately simulate the high frequency performance with the impact of parasitic RLC and layout dependent effects. Also, the equivalent circuits with scalable model parameters for finger numbers can be easily implemented for high frequency circuit simulation and design.

articleTitle: Cryogenic Single-Chip Multi-Channel LNA
abstract: This paper presents the integration of multiple cryogenic low-noise amplifiers (LNAs) on a single chip designed for superconducting nanowire single photon detector (SNSPD) readout. The five-channel LNA ICs were fabricated in a 0.13-µm SiGe BiCMOS technology and tested in 4-K physical temperature using an on-wafer RF probing method.

articleTitle: High-Sensitivity 270-320 GHz InGaAs-Based Power Detector with Temperature-Compensation Mechanism
abstract: This paper presents the design and measured performance of the first power detector tailored for power monitoring in communication systems operating in the frequency range of 270 GHz to 320 GHz. State-of-the-art sensitivity of 2.5 kV/W for a 300 GHz sinusoidal signal and state-of-the-art layout compactness with a 300 um to 200 um core size are achieved. The high sensitivity is reached by utilizing a reduced conduction angle of 140° of a common-source InGaAs mHEMT-based amplifier. A temperature-compensation mechanism is included in the compact core of the design and its performance is investigated in the range of 298 K to 338 K.

articleTitle: Prediction of the Large-Signal GaN HEMT Performance Using Accurate TCAD-Compact Modeling Method
abstract: Accurate prediction of the large-signal power performance of gallium nitride (GaN) high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) can be achieved by combining TCAD device modeling with the RF simulations of a physics-based compact model, equipped with a precise trap description. A TCAD computational framework well-calibrated with small-signal and drain-lag measurements from an AlGaN/GaN device served as an input for compact model extraction. The validity of the approach is confirmed through comparison with measurements on devices with different dimensions and locations on the wafer.

articleTitle: Switch Integrated Ka-Band Low Noise Amplifier in GaN/AlN HEMT Technology
abstract: This paper presents low noise amplifiers (LNA) with integrated DC and RF switching features for multifunctional single chip RF front end (RFFE) applications. Two 28–32 GHz LNAs, with and without integrated switch, are fabricated using 150 nm GaN/AlN HEMT technology. An innovative approach of RF switch integration in the LNA is reported promising compact switch integrated LNA chips. The integrated DC supply switch turns off the DC supply of the idle LNA in the transmit mode of half-duplex operation. The measured LNA without switch demonstrates S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> of 15.8–16.3 dB, noise figure less than 3.6 dB, OP1dB of 12.8 dBm and OIP3 of 25 dBm. In the receive mode, the switch integrated LNA shows S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> of 12.5–13.7 dB, noise figure less than 4.8 dB, OP1dB of 12.5 dBm and OIP3 of 25.8 dBm. In the transmit mode, the LNA bias current sinks from mA- to µA-range and the small-signal performance having S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> higher than 3 dB and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> less than −35 dB indicates the switch integrated−LNA befitting for RFFEs.

articleTitle: A 27 GHz GaN MMIC Doherty Power Amplifier with Optimized Driver Stages
abstract: In this work, a 26.5 GHz to 29 GHz GaN MMIC Doherty power amplifier concept with two stages per path is investigated in a 150 nm GaN HEMT MMIC technology. Prior to the design the placement of driver stages in Doherty amplifiers is studied and their influence on the system efficiency is evaluated. One of the key findings is that a gain in the second stage of 15 dB assures a degradation on system drain efficiency of less than 5 % in comparison to the single stage efficiency of the second stage. The fabricated GaN Doherty amplifier exhibits a maximum power added efficiency of 35 % and maximum backoff efficiency of 24 % at 8 dB backoff while maintaining a saturated output power of 30.4 dBm.

articleTitle: Pseudo-vertical GaN-on-Sapphire PiN Diode: Process Optimizations and Electrical Properties
abstract: In this study, pseudo-vertical GaN-on-Sapphire PiN diodes with different mesa radii were designed, fabricated and characterized. First, critical process stages, such as mesa etching, ohmic contacts on GaN and passivation, are presented and reviewed to obtain functional diodes. Ion beam etching, with an optimized USG hard mask, seems the best solution to achieve reliable devices. Our results also show the impact of different passivation solutions on Au/Ni ohmic contact. Finally, the diodes with varying radii of the mesa (20, 40 and 60 μm) exhibit turn-on voltages of approximately 3.5 V and achieve a specific onresistance of 0.56-1.7 mΩ·cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. More, the devices show low capacitance versus frequency properties up to 40GHz. Further adjustments on designs and fabrication processes are requested to enhance performance.

articleTitle: GaN Schottky Diodes Parameter Extraction Model from S-Parameters Measurement
abstract: GaN-on-sapphire Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) have been fabricated for frequency multiplier applications. A complete set of characterization has been done, including DC and RF measurements. A model to extract the Schottky parameters from S-parameters measurements in small diodes is proposed, obtaining good capacitance agreement compared with that extracted from capacitance-voltage (C-V) measurements carried out in large-area diodes where the parasitic effects are not significant.

articleTitle: A 20-46 GHz 28nm FD-SOI CMOS Tunable Twisted Hybrid Coupler with Cross-Coupled Capacitor Banks for 5G Applications
abstract: A 20-46 GHz quadrature twisted hybrid coupler with a high relative bandwidth of 79 % and low insertion losses is presented in this paper. The hybrid coupler uses an innovative tunable 3-bit architecture with two cross-coupled capacitor banks and offers eight operating modes, enabling it to select the desired center frequency between 22.5 and 43 GHz. The hybrid coupler achieves an insertion loss lower than 1.95 dB with a minimum of 1.05 dB at 22.5 GHz and a phase difference between its two output paths of 91 ± 5°. The circuit is implemented in a CMOS 28nm FD-SOI process and occupies 0.00458 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Efficient Output Power Configuration in a K-Band Power Amplifier Using a Split-Gate Layout
abstract: A multi-finger RF transistor has been divided into multiple gate sections which can be biased independently. This provides a system designer the ability to dynamically reconfigure the output power and power gain of the device while maintaining good power efficiency and without changing the input drive power. By selectively switching the gate biases below pinch-off to effectively reduce the device’s active periphery, the maximum current of the device can be tuned to "follow" a reduced drain bias voltage, so that the optimum impedance at lower power remains similar to the one at full power, and a fixed matching network can be used to accommodate all power modes. The concept has been implemented in a K-Band PA prototype. Simulation show the achievement of two power modes, with ≃6dB of maximum output power tuning while maintaining an efficiency >35% in both modes. Initial small signal measurement results show the tuning capability being effective in tuning the gain of the PA.

articleTitle: Cascaded 4:1 AMUX-DAC Using Novel Clocking and Advanced DSP
abstract: The analog bandwidth of digital-to-analog converters (DACs) implemented in CMOS, which are generally used in commercial optical transmission systems, has been stagnating in recent years with new technology nodes. A promising concept enabling higher signal bandwidths is cascaded analog multiplexing (AMUX). In this work, we discuss the system-level aspects of a 4:1 cascaded AMUX and propose a novel clocking scheme, combining multiple advantages of previous methods. Successively, we use the scheme to demonstrate PAM-4 and PAM-8 signal generation at 60GBd using advanced DSP, quadrupling the sample rate of four DAC-generated signals with three 2:1, 130nm SiGe AMUX modules.

articleTitle: A 225 GHz 90-nm SiGe Coupled-Line Coupler Gain-Boosted Low Noise Amplifier Operating Above fmax/2
abstract: This work presents two low noise amplifiers (LNA) operating at 225 GHz utilizing a novel coupled-line coupler gain-boosting technique that achieves increased power gain compared to conventional common-emitter stages with no additional power consumption. This technique is demonstrated and fabricated in a 90 nm SiGe BiCMOS process technology. The seven-stage and 15-stage LNAs operating at 225 GHz exhibit a measured gain of 5 dB and 11.7 dB, respectively. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this work demonstrates the first implementation of a coupled-line coupler based gain-boosting technique for use in sub-THz amplifiers operating above f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>/2.

articleTitle: A Dual Function 300-GHz FMCW Radar and Communication Transceiver Based on a SiGe MMIC
abstract: A 300 GHz transceiver with two operating modes is presented. The FMCW radar mode enables high precision measurements, while the communication mode enables the transmission of modulated signals in the THz frequency range. The transceiver is based on a custom developed MMIC fabricated in Infineon’s B12HFC SiGe process with an f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf> of 300 GHz and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> of 600 GHz. In this paper we focus on the radar mode of operation, which achieves a spacial resolution of 3.9 mm with a frequency sweep from 330 GHz to 240 GHz in 5 ms for a target at 0.5 m distance.

articleTitle: Investigation of Thermal Resistance Extraction of GaN HEMTs through DCT Measurements Techniques and TCAD-Based Physical Simulations
abstract: In this paper, we extract the thermal resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>) of an AlGaN/GaN HEMT using a simple approach based on Drain Current Transient (DCT) spectroscopy technique. Previous work confirms that acceptor-like traps present in the Fe-doped GaN buffer are responsible for the drain-lag effect observed in the measurement. The main goal of this work is the use of trap emission time constant which is very sensitive to temperature. The extracted R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf> using the new approach was around 13 °C.mm/W. TCAD confirms that the R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf> determined using the new measurement approach represents the R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf> located around 150 nm under the gate.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Millimeter-Wave Avalanche Noise Diodes in Different Si Technologies
abstract: Solid-state noise sources are essential components in highly reliable mm-wave systems for life- or mission-critical applications such as self-driving car radars, airborne and satellite communication systems, space science instruments, and 6G to THz communications. Integrating a noise source, typically based on the avalanche effect of diode junctions, allows for testing of the architecture during production and operational lifetime. This paper presents a comparative study of three avalanche noise diodes integrated in different silicon technologies. The study is based on a solid experimental work that highlights the key points for a successful device design aimed at increasing the generated noise power, bandwidth, and operating frequency.

articleTitle: Ultra-broad Band RF Switches Based on Multilayers MoS2
abstract: Nonvolatile switching phenomena have been observed in various monolayer and multilayers two-dimensional (2D) materials over the past several years. Previous works show that this phenomenon can be exploited to make RF switches for high-frequency data communication thanks to its large band operation. First, we describe the structure of our radio frequency (RF) non-volatile MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> switches, its functioning and its static current–voltage characteristics (I-Vs). The device exhibits an isolation of -30 dB in OFF state at 65 GHz and an insertion loss of –1.5 dB in ON state at 65 GHz for 3 monolayers (MLs). We present the de-embedding method used to extract the device's R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf> and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> values. For 0.5x0.5 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> active part device, we obtained an average of 15.5 Ω and 0.58 fF for 6 MLs device and an average of 13.6 Ω and 1.15 fF for 3 MLs device as R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf> and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> respectively. Few devices were also measured up to 750 GHz. They exhibit a S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> parameters of -15 dB and -5 dB at 650 GHz in OFF and ON state. Keywords — RF switch, 2D materials, De-embedding

articleTitle: A Compact K-Band High Data Rate Upconverter / Solid State Power Amplifier (SSPA) Downlink Engineering Model for LEO Missions
abstract: An engineering model of a Ka-Band transmitter downlink module for LEO satellites has been developed. The module consists of a custom MMIC chipset, LO circuit module, RF filtering and associated module control electronics. The MMIC chipset consists of an IF attenuator, up-converter, driver MPA and HPA. The HPA exhibits a peak output power of approximately 41dBm with an associated PAE of 25% in the 25.5-27GHz band. The MPA has a small-signal gain of greater than 27dB with an output power > 31dBm. The up-converter MMIC has a conversion gain of approximately 25dB with compliant spurious performance and the attenuator MMIC provides 6-bit control. The MMICs are mounted onto a 4-layer RF substrate and copper inserts provide a low thermal resistance between the package and module baseplate. The output from the MMIC PCA feeds a PCBWR34 transition mounted underneath the PCA, this in turn feeds the waveguide filter. The DC power consumption is 55W from 28V.

articleTitle: A 170-260 GHz SiGe Frequency Doubler with 5-dBm Output Power and 13-dB Input Power Range
abstract: A frequency doubler in a 90-nm SiGe BiCMOS technology operates over 170-260 GHz and incorporates bias feedback to maintain fixed gain over a wider input power range. With a peak conversion gain of -2.0 dB at 190 GHz, the doubler’s bias feedback maintains conversion gain variation to less than 3 dB over a 13-dB input power range. The measured output power is greater than -3.3 dBm over 170-260 GHz, with a peak value of 5.8 dBm and 7.2% efficiency at 206 GHz. The total chip area is 0.074 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and is much more compact than typical doublers.

articleTitle: A D-Band Mixer-First Receiver in 22-nm FD-SOI CMOS with Back-Gate Biasing for I/Q Imbalance Optimization
abstract: A D-band mixer-first receiver in CMOS 22-nm FDSOI with I/Q imbalance optimization is proposed in this paper. The optimization mechanism is implemented on I/Q mixers through adjusting back-gate voltages of the super-low threshold voltage (SLVT) transistors, resulting in a 36.1-dB image-rejection ratio (IRR) at 145 GHz. With a power consumption of 36.9 mW, the receiver achieves a conversion gain (CG) of 18.6 dB and a double-sideband (DSB) noise figure of 15.6 dB at 140 GHz. For zero-IF down-conversion, the proposed I/Q optimization shows EVM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RMS</inf> improvement of 5.6 dB with a 16-QAM 500-MBd signal. Meanwhile for low-IF down-conversion, the receiver supports 64-QAM signal with a data rate of 7.2 Gb/s.

articleTitle: Free-standing Lateral AlGaN/GaN Schottky Barrier Diode Based-on GaN-on-Si Technology for High Microwave Power Applications
abstract: This paper presents the development of a lateral AlGaN/GaN Schottky barrier diode (SBD) on free-standing GaN epilayers achieved through Si substrate removal for GaN-on-Si technology. Compared to conventional SBDs on GaN-on-Si, the newly developed free-standing AlGaN/GaN SBDs exhibit enhanced RF performance (cut-off frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>) and ideality factor (η<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>) without compromising DC performance. DC results reveal an onset voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>) of 1.34 V, on-resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>) of 1.6 Ω•mm, and η<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> of 1.7 (14% improvement). Reverse-breakdown voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">BV</inf>) exceeds 30 V, with a reverse-bias leakage current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf>) below 38 μA/mm. RF performance demonstrates a f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> of 80.2 GHz at zero-bias (11.14% enhancement). The impact of lossy Si substrate coupling effects on RF performance for both SBD structures was studied using 3D-EM simulations for further performance optimisation. These findings imply integrated GaNbased SBDs on Si technology are suitable for high-power and high-temperature system applications at millimetre-wave frequencies, particularly in conjunction with high-thermal coefficient materials such as diamond and AlN.

articleTitle: GaN FET Current Change and Recovery During and After Gamma Radiation
abstract: GaN FET devices are measured, not only before and after, but also during exposure to cobalt-60 gamma radiation. Threshold voltage and drain-gate current variations are observed from CW measurements and the threshold shift compared to control devices. Uniquely, pulsed measurements are also utilised. Results suggest that the effect of the radiation is simple heating.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Two-Port Cascode Self-Mixing Mixer in 130 nm SiGe for Use in Incoherent Radar
abstract: An active unbalanced two-port mixer in 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology is presented which features an ultra-wideband RF input and measured conversion gain of up to 6 dB from 68 to 86 GHz in the E-band with a low power consumption of 55 mW. The mixer is designed specifically for incoherent radar which allows stand-alone operation of radar receivers since synchronization to a transmitted signal is not required. This paper concentrates on the characterization of a two-port self-mixing mixer utilizing two-tone CW measurements in K- and E-band. The ultra-wideband RF bandwidth of the self-mixing mixer allows the use of large bandwidth FMCW chirps for a potentially high radar range resolution. The presented two-port cascode mixer employs a novel circuit topology that is comparable to additive mixers, dedicated to high conversion gain-bandwidth performance.

articleTitle: Optimization of the melt and quench behavior of phase-change RF switch to improve power handling
abstract: This paper presents two methods to improve the reliability and the melting/quench behavior of phase change materials (PCM) used in radiofrequency (RF) switches. Results show benefits of the addition of an aluminum nitride heat spreading layer and the reduction of the distance between the substrate and the PCM. The reduction of the PCM cooling time shown in simulations and the power handling improvement observed in measurements on series structures support our proposed designs of GeTe based switches with RF gaps lengths over 4μm, allowing the power handling going to reach 31dBm in both ON and OFF states.

articleTitle: Benchmark of Cosimulation Methodologies for Digital Predistortion on IC Wideband Power Amplifiers
abstract: Exploring millimeter-wave bands presents fresh opportunities for new high data rates communication standards, yet confronts technological challenges like power amplification. Digital predistortion (DPD) offers a solution to enhance the linearity of the amplification while keeping high efficiency. Since Envelope Transient simulations (ET) are time-consuming during circuit design, designers often restort to experimental DPD verification instead. This paper proposes two co-simulation workflows to simulate modulated signals on Integrated Circuits (IC) Power Amplifiers (PA) with an application of DPD. Simulation results indicate that the computational modeling of power amplifiers enables 99% faster schematic and post-layout (PLS) ET simulations, reducing the time needed from months to minutes while maintaining comparable output accuracy.

articleTitle: Proposing a Subharmonic Downconverting IQ-Mixer for mm-Wave 6G and Other D-Band Applications
abstract: Modern communication systems are driven to increasingly higher operating frequencies to maximize absolute bandwidth and thereby data rate. However, getting closer to the technologies f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>, signal generation becomes increasingly inefficient. Especially generating the high amplitude LO signal for downconverting mixers, which are a key component in communication systems, is affected by this inefficiency. Therefore, we propose a fully differential subharmonic downconversion IQ mixer in a 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology to enable efficient generation of the LO signal subharmonicly. A measured image rejection ration of up to 26.3 dB is achieved and demonstrates a differential, subharmonic IQ-mixer in the D-Band. It offers maximum conversion gain of 4.5 dB at a supply voltage of 3.3 V and a power consumption of 67 mW.

articleTitle: A 100-114 GHz GaAs MMIC Power Amplifier With Fully Integrated Dynamic Gate Bias Control for Linearization and Efficiency Enhancement
abstract: This paper presents a dynamically gate-biased MMIC power amplifier (PA) operating in the 100 to 114 GHz frequency range and designed using a 100 nm GaAs pHEMT process. The design comprises a PA, power detector, controller, and gate bias driver - thus fully implementing a dynamically gate-biased PA with programmable complex gain characteristics. The paper demonstrates successful dynamic control over power consumption and gain of the PA through the integrated dynamic gate bias circuit. Quasi-static simulations based on the measured AM/AM and AM/PM responses demonstrate that, at the spectrum emission mask limit, with integrated dynamic gate biasing, the PA achieves a 1.67 dB increase in average output power and its average power added efficiency (PAE) with a 4QAM signal was increased by 20% when compared for static biasing. To the best of our knowledge, this represents the first millimeter-wave fully MMIC-integrated dynamic gate-biased power amplifier in an III-V pHEMT process.

articleTitle: Design and Performance of Slow-wave Microstrip Lines in BiCMOS Technology
abstract: In this article, we present an innovative slow-wave line concept based on a recently published idea that we have simplified. This concept relies on the use of microstrip lines, making it highly suitable for the implementation of mixed microstrip and slow-wave circuits. Different configurations of layers in the considered CMOS technology have been investigated for better performance of the proposed slow-wave microstrip line. A slow-wave factor of 1.4 can be achieved, translating to length reduction factor of 40%. The width of the strips, for the same characteristic impedance of 50 Ω, is reduced by approximately a factor of 3, allowing for more aggressive meandering, leading to more compact layouts. The quality factor is about half of a conventional microstrip line having the same characteristic impedance, but remains significant beyond 100 GHz.

articleTitle: A Wideband Millimeter-wave Vector-Sum Phase shifter in 28-nm bulk CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a wideband vector-sum phase shifter (VSPS) operating within 21-43.9 GHz, implemented in TSMC 28-nm bulk CMOS. The VSPS comprises a quadrature all-pass filter (QAF) with a compensation network, a vector modulator with a compensation amplifier, and input and output wideband matching networks. Simulated phase and gain imbalances of the QAF are below 1.6° and 1 dB, respectively. Measured results of the proposed VSPS exhibit a peak gain of 1.8 dB (inclusive of input and output baluns), with a 3-dB bandwidth of 21-43.9 GHz and a DC power consumption of 38.7 mW. The measured RMS phase error and gain error are 0.75° to 1.25° and 0.57 dB to 1.35 dB, respectively. The core chip area is 0.34 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The circuit can cover mainstream communication frequency bands with a good performance, making it a promising candidate for practical applications.

articleTitle: K/Ka-Band Integrated Duplexer for SatCom on the Move User Terminals
abstract: The design and test of a package-integrated duplexer for K/Ka-Band Satcom on the move user terminals is presented. The proposed structure is very compact and it is embedded into a package stackup. Two elliptic bandpass filters, one for TX and one for RX bandwidths have been used to provide wider and lower out-of-band suppression and good standing wave ratio. Simulated and measured results demonstrate that the proposed duplexer can be very suitable for Satcom systems in K/Ka-band, as its compactness will provide easy feasibility for the integration with RF chips and antenna elements to realize an Antenna Front End (AFE).

articleTitle: 230-GHz SPDT Switch with 60-GHz Bandwidth and 20 dB Dynamic Ratio Utilizing Double-Shunt Topology in SiGe BiCMOS
abstract: This paper presents the analysis and design of a single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS technology with an operating frequency from 200 GHz to 260 GHz. The switch design is based on the λ/4-shunt topology, and optimized for a high dynamic ratio by introducing a double shunt transistor with increased internal impedance level for matching. The tradeoff between insertion loss (IL), isolation, dynamic ratio and bandwidth is discussed. The switch achieves an IL of 4.6 dB to 6.0 dB, isolation of 15 dB to 26.3 dB, and consumes 0.12-mW DC power in measurements. With a dynamic ratio of 20 dB in the frequency band of 220 GHz, the switch shows a comparable performance to the designs in III-V technologies. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, the presented SPDT switch achieves the highest operating frequency in silicon-based process.

articleTitle: mm-Wave GaN Varactors and E/W-Band Phase Shifter
abstract: In this paper, we characterize and compare novel anti-series GaN varactors of three different gate lengths for use at mm-wave frequencies beyond 50 GHz. We focus on insertion loss and phase steering capability versus bias range. The results show a capacitance ratio of up to 7.8 for the longest gates and a tradeoff between capacitance ratio and insertion loss. The devices were implemented in an established GaN MMIC technology, allowing co-design with other circuit features. Using the results of this study, we also develop a mm-wave phase shifter MMIC that operates in a wide frequency range from 50 to 110 GHz and enables phase offsets of up to 114°.

articleTitle: A 22-nm FDSOI 35-41 GHz Frequency Synthesizer
abstract: This paper proposes a 35 to 41 GHz frequency synthesizer based on programmable integer-N frequency multiplication offering perfect synchronization with the input reference signal and precise phase control of the output signal. A prototype fabricated in a 22-nm FDSOI technology is presented with phase noise at 1 MHz offset frequency of -97 dBc/Hz, state of the art power and tuning range figures of merit of 174 dBc/Hz and 177 dBc/Hz, respectively, and a power consumption of 32 mW.

articleTitle: A 24 GHz 14 W/22 W GaN Power Amplifier MMICs for Millimeter Wave band Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: This paper presents the design and measurement of a 24 GHz band 14 W/22 W output power and 36.3%/29% power added efficiency (PAE) GaN power amplifier (PA) microwave monolithic integrated circuits (MMICs) for millimeter wave band wireless power transfer. The GaN PA MMICs are fabricated on a 50 μm thick SiC using a 0.15 μm gate-length GaN process. A three-stage cascaded PA with a low-loss output circuit and a balanced PA with Lange coupler us realized, which achieves excellent output power and PAE. The fabricated single-ended and balanced GaN PA MMIC achieves 41.5 dBm (14.1 W) and 43.6 dBm (22.9 W) of continuous wave (CW) output power and PAEs of 36.3% and 29% in 24 GHz.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band Reconfigurable Output Power PA MMIC
abstract: The design and experimental results for a 4-level GaAs Ka-band output power reconfigurable amplifier MMIC is presented. The PA delivers up to 1.0W of CW power when set to the maximum power mode. The MMIC can be electronically reconfigured for output powers of 1.0W, 0.75W, 0.5W and 0.25W. The small gain and return loss over the 17.3-20.2GHz design band is typically 18dB and less than -10dB respectively. The power added efficiency exceeds 30% for all 4 power settings and the AM/AM and AM/PM characteristics track between the power levels. The output power is reconfigured via three 0V/-4V control lines. An on-chip bias circuit automatically deactivates the appropriate unused amplifier channels without any alteration or adjustment of the drain voltage supply. Since the power levels are electronically reconfigurable this amplifier MMIC enables the possibility of dynamic amplitude taper adjustment for an operating antenna array.

articleTitle: An E-Band, High-Gain Current Clamping Power Amplifier for eWLB-Integration
abstract: This work presents a 2-stage, class AB Power Amplifier (PA) in Infineon’s 130nm b11hfc technology, prepared for the integration in an eWLB package. It employs a cascode stage and a transformer to feed an output stage in a double common base configuration based on the current clamping principle. The PA operates within 22GHz of 3-dB bandwidth (62.2GHz-84.2GHz) in the E-band, outputting a maximum power of 15dBm at the automotive frequency of 76GHz. With its current draw of 47.5mA from a 3.3V supply for a total power consumption of 156.75mW in saturation, a PAE of 19.5% was calculated. Regarding linearity, an OP1dB of 13.6dBm at an IP1dB of -15.8dBm was achieved. This early saturation is accompanied by 33dB of small signal gain, leading to a high versatility for e.g. the automotive industry. The core size of the chip is only 440µm x 400µm (0.176mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), and 930µm x 930µm (0.87mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) including the pad frame, the input/output baluns and thermal contacts.

articleTitle: A Low Power Cascaded Eight-Channel D-Band Receiver using Single LO Mixer and On-Chip Feeder in 40-nm CMOS for Massive Array FMCW Radar
abstract: This paper introduces a 120 GHz low power four-channel receiver chip and cascaded antenna integrated eight-channel receiver module implemented in a 40nm CMOS process. On-chip antenna feeder and reference LO repeater are implemented to facilitate the antenna and multi-chip integration without complex and expensive packaging processes. The proposed receiver consists of high multiplying ratio (×32) frequency multiplier with reference LO repeater, a four-stage low noise amplifier (LNA), single LO mixer (SLM), transimpedance amplifier (TIA), and baseband amplifier (BBA). To demonstrate multichannel scalability, two receiver chips are cascaded using LO repeater to form an eight-channel receiver module, which is fully packaged with antennas. The over the air test of the eight-channel antenna integrated receiver module demonstrates a peak gain of 62.6 dB, while consuming 370 mW, 46.3 mW per each channel.

articleTitle: Low-Power mm-Wave Frequency Quadrupler Using Deep Class-C Doublers
abstract: In this paper, a low-power mm-wave frequency quadrupler is introduced. The proposed quadrupler comprises two push-push frequency doublers operating in deep class-C mode to ensure minimal static power consumption. The quadrupler is fabricated in the 22-nm FD-SOI process technology and uses an area of 0.5×0.41mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It generates a ≈ 60 GHz signal with a P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">out</inf> of -10 dBm from a 15 GHz input signal and provides 10.8GHz output bandwidth (18% fractional bandwidth). Its low power consumption and wide bandwidth make it attractive for many operations in the 60GHz spectrum, including advanced communication with a high data rate. Operating from 54.9− 65.7GHz, its total power consumption is 12 mW, which includes the output pad driver; however, the core frequency quadrupler consumes only 5 mW due to deep class-C operation.

articleTitle: Robust Small-to-Large Signal Transition Extrapolation for ANN-based Transistor Models
abstract: This work proposes a pre-processing technique to improve the small-to-large signal extrapolation in an ANN-based behavioral model for packaged transistors. By using the proposed technique, it is possible to use the large-signal load-pull measurements of the device together with its S-parameters and guarantee a robust transition to the small-signal region, which is useful in the simulation of complex PA architectures. The proposed model was tested for a very high-power class-C biased GaN HEMT, in a commercial harmonic balance simulator, both in single-ended and sequential load-modulated balanced amplifier configurations.

articleTitle: 12 GHz Stacked Power Amplifier with 22.9 dBm Psat and 44.9% PAEsat for 6G in 22nm FDSOI
abstract: This paper presents a stacked power amplifier (PA) operating in the 6G Frequency Range 3 (FR3) band. With three stacked transistors and a V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</inf> of 2.4V, this PA achieves a P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf> of 22.9 dBm and a PAE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf> of 44.9% at 12 GHz. When tested under a 100 MHz single-carrier 64-QAM signal at 12 GHz, this PA achieves an average output power of 18.5 dBm and an average PAE of 31% at an EMV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rms</inf> of -25.1 dB. With a 100 MHz 256-QAM signal, this PA achieves P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">avg</inf> of 16.8 dBm and PAE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">avg</inf> of 25%. Multiple chip samples have been tested to validate the measurement results. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a silicon PA supporting high-speed complex modulation with high efficiency for the 6G FR3 band. This PA design also showcases the best modulation efficiency for 64-QAM and 256-QAM among silicon PA designs in the same frequency range. Furthermore, this design achieves a 1W/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> power density with only a 2.4V supply.

articleTitle: A 23.9 dBm Q-Band Power Amplifier in 22nm FD-SOI Using Resonated Amplifier Cores
abstract: This paper presents a 34 to 42 GHz power amplifier (PA) in GlobalFoundries’ 22 nm fully-depleted silicon on insulator (FDSOI) technology. The amplifier provides a saturated output power of 23.9 dBm from a 1.6 V supply at 38 GHz, while achieving a peak power added efficiency (PAE) of 20.8 %. This high output power is enabled by applying a novel PA core design method for large PAs to this technology. The PA achieves an average PAE of 6.2 % at -25 dB EVM for a 2.4Gb/s 64-QAM input signal at 38 GHz.

articleTitle: On the Equivalence of Network Representations in Relation to Stability Analysis
abstract: The precise relations between number of RHP zeros and poles of the characteristic determinants in the three main representations (impedance, admittance and scattering) are derived. Given one inherently-stable representation, formulas are provided to predict the numbers of RHP zeros and poles of the characteristic determinants in the other representations. Finally, it is shown that, if at least one out the impedance and admittance representations fulfills the proviso, then some inherently-stable scattering representation also exists.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide in 3D Integrated Technology for D-Band Applications
abstract: A Substrate Integrated Waveguide developed in a 3D technology and implemented between two silicon dies is presented. This waveguide was designed to operate in the millimeter D-Band (110 GHz – 170 GHz). This first fabrication allows the validation of both the design and the proposed 3D technology for millimeter-wave applications. Indeed, a similar frequency behavior can be observed in the simulation and measurement results.

articleTitle: A 76-81 GHz Variable Gain Power Amplifier in 16 nm FinFET CMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents a power amplifier (PA) in the 76-81 GHz automotive radar band, implemented in an advanced 16 nm FinFET CMOS node. The PA consists of 3 common-source (CS) neutralized differential pairs (NDP) and transformer-based matching networks. The first two stages allow digital gain and current consumption control. The last stage utilizes power combining to boost the output power while adhering to the stringent reliability constraints. The PA delivers a measured saturated output power of 13.2-14 dBm across the 76-81 GHz band. It achieves measured small signal gain in full gain mode of 30.7-32.3 dB in that band and gain tuning range of 33 dB. The PA occupies core area of 460 µm x 150 µm and consumes 130 mA from 0.95 V supply in saturation.

articleTitle: A compact 47 GHz Band 2×16ch CMOS Phased Array Transceiver Chip with Bi-directional IF Phase Shifter and IQ Mixer
abstract: This paper presents a 4 × 4 vertical and horizontal polarized compact 47GHz fully integrated CMOS transceiver with bi-directional IF phase shifter, IQ mixer and Antenna in Package (AiP) technology. The proposed bi-directional IF phase shifter and IQ mixer realized less than 1.0° phase resolution with rms phase error of 0.447° and rms amplitude error of 0.063 dB, and the output third-order intercept point above +1.0 dBm with TX conversion gain more than 16.5 dB in the RF frequency ranges from 46-49 GHz. TX EVM of a transceiver chip under 5G NR modulation (100 MHz BW, 256-QAM OFDM) achieves less than -27.5 dB with a delivered output power of +7.5 dBm at 47 GHz. The AiP consists of a 4x4 array of 16 patch antennas and transceiver chip. The finalized AiP features 12.3 × 14.9 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in dimensions and the proposed transceiver chip is only 9.1 × 11.7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Ka-Band Cascode CMOS Power Amplifier with Improved Linearity Using Bias Optimization Technique
abstract: In this study, we presented a bias optimization design technique to maximize the linearity of the cascode power amplifier. Optimization was performed based on distortion and IMD3 analysis through continuous wave and two-tone power simulation. The proposed optimization design technique was validated through measurements with 64-quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) signals, which had a 100-MHz channel bandwidth. The designed differential cascode power amplifier, using a 65-nm RF CMOS process, achieved an output 1-dB compression point (OP1dB) of 17.0-dBm, a saturation output power (PSAT) of 18.5-dBm, and a peak power-added efficiency (PAE) of 32.7% at 28 GHz. Furthermore, the 64-QAM performance achieved a PAVG of 11.7-dBm and a PAEAVG of 16% with —25 dB error vector magnitude (EVM) and the adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR) of —28.7 dBc. Through the bias optimization technique, PAVG and PAEAVG were improved by 1.1-dBm and 2.4%, respectively.

articleTitle: A Novel Stability Margin for Transfer Functions
abstract: This work presents a novel stability margin function for use with nodal driving point impedance and admittance transfer functions. Unlike a loop gain or NDF, the nodal driving point transfer functions themselves have units of impedance or admittance whose values are very circuit design dependent, making uniform applicability to all nodes within a circuit, for the purpose of assessing stability margin, impossible. Fortunately, the driving point transfer functions are fundamentally composed of the sum of bidirectional looking impedances or admittances which can then be used to construct a unitless, normalized, proxy function that can be successfully used for stability margin assessment. This new stability margin function is applied to a parametric oscillation discovered in a measured amplifier originally simulated to be stable.

articleTitle: Analysis of mm-Wave Detection with AlGaN/GaN HEMTs by means of Measurements and Physical and Equivalent Circuit Models
abstract: The responsivity of microwave zero-bias detectors based on GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) is measured up to 67 GHz and compared with Monte Carlo (MC) simulations. In addition, a predictive analytical closed-box model based on the measurement (or MC calculation) of the I-V curves and the S-parameters of the devices is shown to replicate the zero-bias current responsivity. The extraction of the HEMT Small-Signal Equivalent Circuit (SSEC) is also exploited to evaluate the responsivity with such closed-form expression. The comparison of the results provided by this approach with the values obtained directly from experiments and MC simulations allows not only to predict the response of the devices at frequencies above the reach of the measurements, but also to identify the physical origin of the detection and the contribution of the different SSEC elements.

articleTitle: Extension of SC-gate FET Concept to 100 GHz Band and Parallel Connection
abstract: This study presents the design and prototype of a GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) in which the standing wave controlled gate (SC-gate) concept is extended to high frequencies. Measurements reveal that the maximum available power gain (MAG) improves from 2 to 9 dB, even in the 100 GHz band. A prototype of a 16-parallelled multifinger GaN HEMT is produced by applying the SC-gate concept to control the standing wave in the parallel wiring of a multifinger GaN HEMT. Measurement results verify that the MAG is improved from 0 to 6 dB at 45 GHz.

articleTitle: Sub-6 GHz RF SPDT Switches Designed in an Advanced 28 nm Fully-Depleted Silicon-on-Insulator Technology with a High Resistivity Substrate
abstract: In this paper two RF switches named as 3-stack and 12-stack are studied. They are designed to have the same overall RON and built using a 28 nm FD-SOI technology atop of different substrate resistivities. A new advanced passivation technique is also used in order to boost the switches’ performance. The 3-stack switch atop of standard Process of Reference (POR) substrate (~15 Ωcm) shows an insertion loss 1.2 dB higher than the same switch atop of high-resistivity (>1 k Ωcm) with advanced passivation technique. Moreover, the 12-stack switch with advanced passivation technique demonstrates 2.5 dB improvement in the insertion loss compared to the same one built on a standard substrate while the isolation remains lower than 20 dB.

articleTitle: Short Term Drift in the Recovery Time of GaN HEMT Switches
abstract: A step stress characterization method is proposed to enable the study of the gradual degradation of memory effect-induced recovery in GaN HEMT switches. This is achieved by characterizing the transition from off- to on-state over time and tracking short-term degradation in the recovery of the insertion loss for decreasing off-state voltages. The method is demonstrated on three different technologies. The results show that the degradation varies between foundry processes, illustrating the merit of the method for evaluating the impact of memory effects in GaN HEMT switch operation.

articleTitle: Advanced Characterization Approaches with Pad-Model De-Embedding of sub-THz Devices for 6G Applications
abstract: This work describes accurate methods for the characterization of sub-terahertz (sub-THz) devices and pad de-embedding procedures. The extraction of the intrinsic DUT is enabled by generating a precise pad model using two-tier calibration approaches. Moreover, the proposed approaches offer a solution to the designers to preserve precious silicon area by presenting a simplified and potentially parameterizable pad model. Employing two different thru-reflect-line (TRL) calibration kits (calKits) together with the DUT on the same die, this research validates the proposed calibration strategies. This paper uses as DUT at J-band, i.e. a Marchand balun, fabricated using IHP SiGe BiCMOS technology with an aluminum back-end-of-line (BEOL), alongside the mentioned calKits. The goal of the paper is to assess the performance of the DUT and validate two de-embedding methods. Moreover, the pad model offers a way for accurate DUT characterization saving silicon area for future optimized designs.

articleTitle: An F-Band Two-Stage Buffer Amplifier Gain-Boosted by Lossy RC-Over-Neutralization with a 16.1 GHz Bandwidth in 22nm FDSOI CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a two-stage millimeter-wave amplifier designed in the 22 nm FDSOI CMOS technology. The low gain of the transistors at frequencies close to f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>/2 necessitates the use of special circuit design techniques to enhance gain per amplifier stage. In this work, we employ the lossy capacitive neutralization technique to increase the maximum available gain, as well as the unilateralized power gain of a two-port. This is an alternative gain-boosting approach to the well-known lossless embedding. A design-approach by lossy capacitive neutralization is presented. To ensure a long lifetime of the circuit and better yield, a reduced supply voltage of 0.6 V is used. The fabricated chip reaches in measurement a saturated output power of -3.8 dBm and offers a gain of 5.2 dB. The circuit consumes 16.2 mW of power and active area of 380 × 255 µm.

articleTitle: Optimum Biasing of SiGe-HBTs to Maximize the Gain Per Current for Power Efficient Amplification
abstract: Transistor biasing for RF-amplifiers typically is based on achieving the highest transistor speed given by the maximum oscillation frequency. However in low-power applications such as active tags achieving the maximum small-signal gain combined with minimum power consumption is desired. Therefore we analytically investigate the existence of a maximum of the realizable gain per collector current of SiGe-HBTs. The obtained observations are subsequently analyzed in simulations and proven in measurements of a differential cascode amplifier. When biasing for the proposed maximum the power consumption of amplifier chains can be decreased significantly without sacrificing small-signal gain therefore increasing efficiency and sustainability.

Author Keywords: silicon germanium heterojunction bipolar transistor (SiGe HBT)

articleTitle: Optical Actuation of GeTe Phase-Change RF Switches at 915nm: Performance Comparison for Different GeTe Sizes and Impact of Cycling
abstract: This paper presents GeTe-based switches for RF applications, reversibly switching between their ON and OFF states thanks to optical activation by irradiation. Contrarily to what has been presented so far, the transition is induced by infrared laser pulses, at λ = 915 nm which is very encouraging for future integration of laser sources and therefore for proposing a fully integrated optical actuation of PCMs switches. This is a new trend as compared to literature work dealing with the other side of the visible spectrum, less suited for optical integration on a die. Our work also reveals the effectiveness of wide and thick PCMs at this wavelength, enabling bi-stable switching at high frequencies up to 40 GHz, with a FoM of 31.5 fs attained despite a poor GeTe conductivity of only 1.85·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> S/m. Furthermore, significant progress as compared to the literature has been made by exceeding 30k cycles with optical actuation.

articleTitle: Temperature Calibrated K-Band Noise Source Employing a COTS Si-Ge HBT
abstract: In this paper a mm-Wave, temperature-calibrated K-band noise source built with commercial on-the-shelf (COTS) components is demonstrated. The proposed source includes a Si-Ge Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor (HBT) using its base-emitter (BE) junction driven into avalanche breakdown, as the main noise-generating element. Excess Noise Ratio (ENR) values reaching 10.8 dB were obtained with a 6.71 mA breakdown current, in a 24 GHz to 32 GHz bandwidth and a 21 °C to 102 °C device temperature excursion, with no impedance matching. A calibration model is also provided, which fits ENR magnitude with an average error less than 0.05 dB, when considering the maximum current and temperature ranges. An ENR drift error of 0.8 dB was instead reported for the uncalibrated source.

articleTitle: 5-55 GHz Watt-level Gallium Nitride Stacked FET Travelling-Wave Power Amplifier
abstract: Two well-known ultra wide-band topologies, the travelling-wave amplifier and the stacked cell, are gainfully employed to demonstrate a decade bandwidth behaviour (5-55 GHz) in conjunction with watt-level saturated output power. The selected technology is OMMIC’s Gallium Nitride on Silicon, featuring the possibility to simultaneously insert 60-nm and 100-nm gate length FETs in the same MMIC.

articleTitle: A Transmitter/Receiver Link for High Data Rate Polymer Microwave Fiber Communication at Y-band
abstract: A Y-band (170-260 GHz) ultra high data rate transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx), are designed and fabricated in a commercial 130 nm silicon germanium (SiGe) BiCMOS process. The link has demonstrated data rates up to 30 Gbps over a one meter polymer microwave fiber (PMF), using a carrier of 237 GHz. This is the first PMF link above 200 GHz reaching a distance of one meter.

articleTitle: A W-band Combined Architecture Passive Phase Shifter in SiGe BiCMOS
abstract: A compact low phase error W-band 6-bit passive phase shifter is presented. The proposed phase shifter architecture consists of a combination of High Pass/Low Pass (HP/LP) filters-based phase shifters, a Reflection Type Phase Shifter (RTPS) with capacitive load and a delay line. To minimize the losses PiN-diodes were utilized as switches, due to their superior performance especially in such high frequencies. This phase shifter was designed and implemented in a 140nm SiGe BiCMOS technology and achieves a phase error rms of 1.97º, a Phase to Gain (P2G) error rms of 0.69 dB in a bandwidth of 92 – 100 GHz. The average loss is 14.61 dB at 96 GHz. The fabricated phase shifter occupies 0.22 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area and dissipates 20.88 mW from a 2.4 V supply for the biasing of the PiN diodes. The achieved performance makes this phase shifter a very good candidate for W-band phased array systems.

articleTitle: A 16 GHz Differential Electrical Balance Duplexer Based on Magnetic-Flux Cancelation for M2M Full-Duplex Communication
abstract: This paper presents a 16GHz fully differential electrical balance duplexer (EBD) for enabling full-duplex communication in rotary machine-to-machine (M2M) interfaces. The EBD employs a differential 4-coil 180° hybrid structure with inherent magnetic flux cancelation to achieve >30dB TX-to-RX isolation over 4GHz bandwidth. TX-to-ANT and ANT-to-RX loss is 4.2dB and 4.9dB, respectively. TX-to-ANT input P1dB is larger than +17dBm whereas TX-to-ANT/ANT-to-RX IIP3s are +28.2/+31.4dBm, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this work achieves the widest isolation BW (fractional) and highest IIP3 among EBDs and circulators reported above 10GHz.

articleTitle: SiGe HBT integrated in a 22 nm FDSOI
abstract: 22 nm BiCMOS process, based on the co-integration of the classical 22 nm FDSOI technology and the SiGe-based NPN vertical HBTs, is reported here. The HBTs are fabricated on a hybrid region on the wafer, where the buried oxide was removed. The CMOS integration was adapted to accommodate the additional HBT process steps and to prevent any high-k oxide contamination, yet to preserve the baseline functionality. The bipolars show peak f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MAX</inf> of around 410 and 490 GHz, respectively. The standard logic nFETs and pFETs display a nearly 100% DC performance matching to the baseline and minimal targeting offset. The BiCMOS process has a very limited impact on the overall logic yield. This first ever high performance SiGe HBT integration in a HKMG CMOS process validates viability for future millimeter-wave range applications.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Modeling of CMOS Compatible SiN/AlN/GaN MIS-HEMT on 200mm Si Operating at mm-Wave Frequencies
abstract: The performance of a CMOS-compatible SiN/AlN/GaN MIS-HEMT on 200mm Silicon substrate with high power capabilities in Ka band is evaluated. The devices show an F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>/F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> of 80/170 GHz for 2x50x0.15 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> topology, along with outstanding and competitive large signal performance compared to GaN/SiC at 40 GHz. The devices demonstrate a power added efficiency PAE of 40% and an output saturated power (Psat) of 6.6 W/mm. To fully benefit from the capabilities of this new technology, an empirical Angelov model was modified to accurately describe the electrical behavior of the devices. The proposed model is validated through 40 GHz load pull measurement/simulation comparison and will be used in designing next MMIC PA (Power Amplifiers) dedicated to Ka-Ku band applications.

articleTitle: RF-Robustness enhancement in AlN/GaN HEMT through AlGaN Back-Barrier: nonlinear model analysis
abstract: In this study, we evaluate the robustness and nonlinear (NL) responses of two variants of AlN/GaN HEMT technology under RF-step stress at 10 GHz. We develop an original NL behavioral modelling approach that includes the self-biasing effect within a unique expression. This method is applied to various gate-to-drain (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GD</inf>) HEMT geometries of the two AlN/GaN processes under study. Our investigation highlights several insights into this promising technology: including remarkable RF robustness demonstrated by handling 10 dB of gain compression without any degradation. We observe that devices with an AlGaN back-barrier exhibit higher drain saturation currents (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DSsat</inf>) as L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GD</inf> increases, whereas those without AlGaN back-barrier show a decrease in I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DSsat</inf>. Consequently, devices with an AlGaN backbarrier present better charge stability within the 2-Dimensional Electron Gas (2-DEG), whereas an earlier gain compression appears for those without back-barrier, and with larger L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GD</inf>. Additionally, slower degradation kinetics are observed in devices with an AlGaN back-barrier before fatal failures. We identify the limitation of the Schottky gate to withstand critical RF power (18 dBm), and this gate RF limitation represents a fatal failure mechanism common to both variants.

articleTitle: A 2.5GHz Series Resonance BAW Oscillator in a 130-nm BiCMOS process with 1kHz-offset Phase Noise <-98dBc/Hz and FOM >208dB
abstract: A 2.5GHz series resonance oscillator in an in-house 3rd generation 130-nm BiCMOS process is proposed. The oscillator uses an indigenous Bulk Acoustic Wave (BAW) resonator as the oscillating element and is mounted on top of the silicon die and co-packaged in a standard plastic mold compound. The oscillator can be driven in a high-FOM very low phase-noise mode with FOM >211dB or a high performance ultra-low phase-noise mode with a close-in phase noise better than -98dBc/Hz at 1kHz offset and FOM >208dB, with a 12kHz-20MHz integrated jitter <7fs.

articleTitle: A 258-to-280-GHz 100-Gb/s CMOS Transmitter Element in 40-nm CMOS
abstract: In order to realize a 300-GHz band 1D phased array transmitter, we present a 300-GHz CMOS transmitter (TX) that has an elongated shape that can be arranged at a narrow pitch and has wide bandwidth. Specifically, by adjusting the gate width of the MOSFETs in an up-conversion mixer, the intermediate frequency (IF) input matching circuit is removed, and a wider bandwidth of the mixer is achieved. Furthermore, by cascading IF amplifier stages, both high gain and broad bandwidth are achieved. The long stubs required to widen the bandwidth of input/output matching circuits are made into loops to reduce the height of the chip. The proposed TX element is fabricated using a 40-nm CMOS process and demonstrated that it achieves a data rate of 100 Gb/s with a 3-dB bandwidth above 22.5 GHz, a center frequency of 268 GHz.

articleTitle: The Impact of Nanoscale CMOS Devices Scaling and Variations on mm-Wave CMOS Performance
abstract: The impact of nanoscale CMOS devices scaling and variations as well as layout dependent effects (LDE) on high frequency performance appears as the most critical challenge to nanoscale devices optimization and modeling for mm-Wave and Sub-THz CMOS circuits simulation and design. This paper presents an extraordinary finding in sub-60 nm devices which can exactly meet the foundry golden die target in terms of IDS and g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> from DC measurement on different dies/lots but exhibit dramatic differences at the high frequency performance, such as f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MAX</inf>. It highlights a fundamental problem with the foundry PDK (Process Design Kit) and compact models which are limited to I-V and C-V curves fitting and become invalid for high frequency simulation. For the first time, a high precision parameters extraction method and analytical models are developed based on high frequency characterization to precisely identify sub-nm or atomic scale variations in nanoscale device parameters and explain the mechanism responsible for very different impact on f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MAX</inf> in mm-Wave domain. This fully high frequency based method can facilitate accurate simulation and prediction of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MAX</inf> subject to nanoscale devices scaling and variations.

articleTitle: Full D-Band GaN Power Amplifier MMIC and Waveguide Module
abstract: In this article, we present a gallium nitride (GaN) power amplifier (PA) monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) and waveguide module that cover the full D-band (110–170 GHz) with a state-of-the-art performance. On-wafer measurements of the balanced ten-stage GaN PA show a small-signal gain of more than 13 dB over the full D-band and a peak output power of 22.6 dBm at 160 GHz. A two-way waveguide module delivers more than 18.5 dBm of output power over the full D-band with a peak of 25 dBm at 120 GHz. To the best of our knowledge, the reported amplifiers show the highest output power within GaN-based circuits beyond 140 GHz. This is also the first demonstration of GaN PAs covering the full D-band.

articleTitle: CMOS-integrated terahertz dielectric near-field sensor
abstract: In this research, we present an electronic near-field sensor designed in 180 nm complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology, specifically tailored for terahertz dielectric spectroscopy. Our sensor utilizes a unique on-chip detection mechanism, which allows to probe the dielectric properties of materials in aqueous solutions. We have achieved superior sensitivity values, positioning our sensor at the forefront of terahertz-related techniques.

articleTitle: A High Integrated 13 W & 36 % PAE Ka band GaN MMIC Power Amplifier for SatCom Applications
abstract: This work presents a 13 W Ka-band GaN High Power Amplifier (HPA) operating in the 27-31.5 GHz bandwidth. This MMIC is developed using the qualified UMS 0.15 μm gate length GaN on 70 μm SiC substrate technology. Measurements in test fixture were performed over temperature in order to assess performance under Continuous Wave (CW) signal. At ambient chip backside temperature (Tb=25 °C), the HPA exhibits a small signal gain of 35 dB with a maximum Pout of 41.8 dBm, and a peak PAE of 32.5 % at 10 dBc for the quiescent bias point of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DQ</inf>=25 V and I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DQ</inf>=60 mA/mm. For V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DQ</inf>=22 V, this PAE increase up to 36 % with a 0.6 dB reduction of Pout. The HPA has a small chip size of 2.8 x 2.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with only three biasing pads on each chip side. This HPA achieves among the best performances in terms of trade-off between Pout, gain, PAE and chip size.

articleTitle: 20W and 20% PAE 2-10 GHz High-Power Amplifier for Multifunction RF Systems Manufactured in Leonardo’s GaN pHEMT 0.25um Technology
abstract: This paper presents the design and measurement of a High Power Amplifier (HPA) for Multifunction RF (MFRF) systems. The amplifier have been designed employing Leonardo’s pHEMT GaN process with 250 nm of gate length (LDO_GN25). The amplifier achieves a mean value of 43 dBm of output power with a mean value of power added efficiency of 20 % in the 2-10 GHz frequency band. This HPA is a suitable amplifier to be integrated in the future Transmit and Receive Modules (TRMs) for Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) systems that include Radar, Electronic Warfare (EW) and Communications (COMMs) capabilities in the same system.

articleTitle: 0.13μm SiGe HBT Linear Power Amplifier for broadband 5G applications (1.8GHz to 5GHz)
abstract: A high linear mono die FEM (Front End Module) 1.8-5GHz is presented in this paper. The FEM consists of a 0.13 μm SiGe BiCMOS broadband power amplifier. The power amplifier circuit adopts a class AB reconfigurable bias over bands with external resistor, broad band output matching network and temperature-insensitive bias technique is used to improve linearity over temperature. Measurements at 5V supply with low quiescent current 80-98mA achieve high gain 39dB with 1dB gain flatness over 600MHz. A high linearity of -49dBc in 5G NR 100MHz modulation signals for output power 15 dBm is achieved with P1dB up to 26dBm.
