articleTitle: A 29.5 GHz Rectifier with 14.5 dB Dynamic Power Range for Energy Harvester Using Vertical Nanowire Tunnel FETs
abstract: To extend the output DC power range of energy harvester from µW to mW, the 29.5 GHz rectifier using vertical nanowire Tunnel Field-Effect Transistor (VNW-TFET) is presented in this paper. Advantaged by the low threshold voltage, very steep characteristics, and its ability to operate below 60mV/decade, VNW-TFET is a promising device in rectifier design for low power applications. By analyzing the relation of the number of nanowires in VNW-TFET and its DC characteristic, the rectification efficiency of the proposed design is approximately 20.1% at the input power of 132 µW. Moreover, its peak efficiency is 49.2% at 20 mW, and the input power range for rectification efficiency higher than 40% is between 1.2 dBm and 15.7 dBm when the number of nanowires in VNW-TFET is 20.

articleTitle: Ultra-scaled GaN HEMTs on Sapphire with fT/fmax = 229/528 GHz and NFmin ~ 1 dB
abstract: With advanced down-scaling technology, GaN HEMTs on the cost-effective sapphire substrate may achieve exceptional RF performance, W-band power performance, and low noise performance, making them suitable for 6G/Terahertz communication. In this study, by employing electron beam lithography, ultra-scaled InAlN/GaN HEMTs on sapphire with T-gates with a gate length of ~50 nm and source-drain distance of ~200 nm were fabricated, achieving an impressive current gain cutoff frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>) of 229 GHz and high power cutoff frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>) of 528 GHz. The W-band loadpull analysis indicated that the devices exhibit a linear gain of 6.7 dB, an output power of 14.4 dBm, and a power-added efficiency of 12.5%. Device scaling resulted in low parasitic resistances, leading to an outstandingly low noise figure of 1 dB across the 25-35 GHz frequency range. To the best of the author’s knowledge, our devices have the highest f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>/f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> and lowest noise figure among GaN HEMTs on sapphire, which are comparable with those state-of-the-art counterparts on SiC substrates.

articleTitle: A Low Phase Noise VCO for 60 GHz Radar Applications with a Direct Transformer-Based Fourth Harmonic Extraction in 28 nm CMOS
abstract: In this paper we present a simple generation of a continuously tunable local oscillator (LO) signal at 56.1-to-65.6GHz. It is realized by a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) using transformer-based fourth harmonic (H4) extraction directly from the core. We show in measurement that the direct H4 extraction approach is not adding any excess phase noise (PN) beyond the expected 20 · log(4) degradation due to the frequency scaling by four. The proposed VCO is realized in 28nm bulk CMOS technology and achieves best measured phase noise of −73.4dBc/Hz at 100kHz offset and −99.8dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset from a 56.1GHz carrier with a continuous frequency tuning range (FTR) of 15.6%. The DC power including VCO and buffer is 11.7mW. The VCO achieves a competitive FOM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> of −188dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: Modelling and Design Aids for Millimetre-Wave Low-Noise Amplifiers
abstract: Successful low-noise amplifier (LNA) design at millimetre-wave relies on accurate device linear noise models together with the availability of high-performance and versatile technologies. While device linear modelling is quite practical even at millimetre-wave, the same cannot be said for noise characterization and modelling. Often the latter can be reasonably performed only up to a few tenths of GHz. A complete device linear and noise modelling strategy, oriented to millimetre-wave LNA design, is provided in this contribution, relying on low-frequency noise characterization and millimetre-wave linear characterization. The effect of source degeneration, often applied in LNA design, above 100 GHz is also evaluated.

articleTitle: A Quadrature Harmonic Rejection Voltage-Domain Mixer with 20 dBm OIP3 and 800 MHz IF Bandwidth
abstract: A wideband harmonic rejection voltage-domain mixer using resistive scaling is presented with excellent linearity and high IF bandwidth. Thin-oxide devices with constant gate-to-source voltages (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf>) are utilized to maximize the switching linearity. A novel switching core topology providing low-impedance IF outputs is proposed to support wideband in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) mixer outputs when loaded by ADCs. Eight LO clock phases, each with a 25 % duty cycle, are on-chip generated for quadrature down-conversion and harmonic rejection (HR). By cleverly activating and organizing the mixer branches, the RF mixer input impedance can be kept perfectly constant throughout all eight clock phases, enhancing the mixer’s linearity. The TSMC 40 nm-CMOS realized mixer reaches 20.9 dBm OIP3 at an IF of 50 MHz with a conversion loss of 22.5 dB. It offers an 800 MHz 3-dB IF bandwidth at a differential capacitive loading of 0.15 pF, with a total power consumption of 40.7 mW drawn from a 1.1 V supply. The mixer targets linear wideband base station observation receiver applications.

articleTitle: Optimum Harmonic Load Prediction for RF Power Amplifier Design Using Polyharmonic Distortion Models
abstract: This paper addresses optimal load reflection coefficient prediction in nonlinear radio frequency (RF) power amplifiers (PAs) under large-signal conditions. Traditional measurement-based black box behavioural models are limited to predicting the optimal load at the fundamental frequency. However, as seen in harmonically-tuned amplifiers, the load at the harmonic frequencies can have a significant impact on output power and efficiency. In this work, an harmonic X–parameter model is extracted from a 10 W Cree CGH40010F GaN HEMT device. For the first time, optimum higher-order harmonic load predictions are reported through a constrained optimisation of this multi-harmonic X–parameter model. The results are validated numerically against measured load-pull data at the fundamental and against data simulated directly from a Cree CGH40010F device model for the higher-order harmonic frequencies. The results show that the extracted X–parameter model can predict, very accurately, the optimum loads at both the fundamental and second harmonic frequency.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency 24-GHz Rectifier MMICs using Schottky Barrier Diodes from Foundry
abstract: In this study, we examined a method to increase the efficiency of rectifier MMICs by layout modification without violating the design rules of the foundry process. Developing a new semiconductor element for mass production is time consuming, which in this study was an optimized Schottky barrier diode (SBD) for microwave wireless power transfer. Therefore, circuit designers select off-the-shelf and conventional SBDs; however, they cannot improve the essential performance of the selected SBD. We analyzed and demonstrated a method to improve the SBD efficiency by reducing its external resistance within the design rules of the foundry process. We also demonstrated rectifier MMICs with 58% conversion efficiency under 25-dBm input power at 24 GHz.

articleTitle: A mm-Wave Two-Stage CMOS LNA Using Noise Cancelling and Post-Distortion Techniques
abstract: A wideband two-stage CMOS low-noise amplifier is proposed for millimeter-wave applications. For the first stage, a noise-canceling path is added in parallel with a main path for a low-noise target. The noise-cancelling condition of the main path is roughly maintained in amplitude by a proper gm ratio, and in phase by slightly shifting central frequency of an LC tank. By applying a post-distortion technique to the second stage, an auxiliary path is appended to tap and cancel distortions of the main path from its output side. Double-peak-coupling resonators bridge the stages for a wideband profile. Experimental results have shown 20 dB peak gain and minimal 3.1 dB NF across the passband of 28-37 GHz. Moreover, the inband third-order input intercept point (IIP3) is shown as -9.4~-2 dBm. Fabricated in a 65 nm CMOS process, the circuit core consumes 17.8 mW with a 1.2 V supply and occupies an area of 869×274 um<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Wideband D-Band Front-end Transmitter Components in a 90-nm SiGe Process
abstract: This paper characterizes two front-end components for a wideband D-band transmitter (TX). First, a three-stage, differential common-emitter (CE) power amplifier (PA) with cross-coupled capacitors offers high gain, unconditional stability, and wideband inter-stage transformers that result in more than 30 GHz of 3-dB power-gain bandwidth. Second, a 2-bit vector-modulated phase shifter (PS) uses one-hot encoding to reduce the number of high-speed control lines per TX channel and ease scaling to large multi-channel arrays. The PA and PS are designed in a 90-nm SiGe HBT process with f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> = 375GHz. The PA reaches a saturated output power of 13.6 dBm with 10.2% power added efficiency (PAE). The phase shifter has an input 1-dB gain compression point (IP1dB) of -4.8 dBm at 135 GHz with root-mean-square (RMS) gain and phase error of 0.7-2.0 dB and 6.1-14.2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> across 115-155 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: A 30 GHz PLL with Automated Frequency Control Option for Robust Operation in Harsh Environments
abstract: This paper presents a fractional-N phase-locked loop (PLL) circuit which offers robust operation at harsh environments and ease of measurement in aging and radiation tests. The PLL includes an automated frequency calibration (AFC) block whose main objective is to monitor the effects of operating conditions on the voltage controlled oscillator (VCO) in a closed-loop operation. The PLL generates frequencies ranging from 29GHz to 34 GHz with a VCO that has two analog capacitive tuning nodes and 16 digitally controlled sub-bands. In the long-term operation, the AFC will compensate frequency shifts in the VCO by autonomous band selection. Also, during aging/radiation tests, the reference input frequency can be swept around 100MHz in a 15 MHz sweep bandwidth while the 4 control bits are written via the AFC circuit. So the whole frequency range can be monitored without disturbing the low gain, analog tuning of the VCO with the measurements performed on the quasi-DC control voltage. Since the measurement relies on the FM demodulation principle, the circuit conveniently eliminates RF signal measurement during test of PLLs in harsh environments.

articleTitle: On the use of TCAD for the thermal analysis of RF power transistors and its application to a GaN-on-SiC HEMT with a diamond composite flange
abstract: This paper reports on the use of TCAD for thermal simulation of GaN-on-SiC HEMT RF power transistors. Firstly, the results are compared with those obtained using ANSYS Mechanical Pro, then the advantages of TCAD for thermal analysis are detailed, and finally it is used to analyze a GaN HEMT on a diamond composite flange which offers a very substantial reduction in thermal resistance. This is believed to be the first report of a kW-level GaN HEMT RF power transistor manufactured on a diamond composite flange.

articleTitle: A 60GHz Cross-Coupled Transformer-Based Quadrature-Phase Coupler in 22nm FD-SOI
abstract: This paper presents and analyses a transformer-based quadrature-phase coupler using a capacitive cross-coupling technique. The transformer-based architecture is preferable for circuit designs for quadrature-phase generation at high frequencies due to its compact size and low loss. However, this approach could suffer from the low magnetic coupling between metal conductors, which is limited by the minimal distance of metal conductors in the technology available. A low magnetic coupling will cause an insufficient coupling coefficient of the coupler leaving an amplitude imbalance at the coupler outputs, which is bad if an equal power division is desired. A novel capacitive cross-coupling technique is introduced in this work. By adding two cross-coupled capacitors diagonally, the overall coupling coefficient of the coupler can be improved. To prove the concept, a 60 GHz circuit is implemented in 22nm FD-SOI (fully-depleted silicon on insulator) CMOS. The measured insertion loss of the proposed coupler is 1.3dB. The measured phase difference between the two output ports is 92° at 60GHz. The coupler achieves an isolation between two outputs of around 30dB at 60GHz. To the best knowledge of the authors, this is the first cross-coupled transformer-based quadrature-phase coupler operating at 60GHz.

articleTitle: A DC to 67-GHz 40-nm CMOS SP4T Switch for Cryogenic S-Parameter Measurement and Calibration
abstract: To improve the accuracy and precision of the cryogenic S-parameter measurement and calibration, a dc to 67-GHz single-pole-four-throw (SP4T) switch is proposed as a core circuitry in the measurement system. This broadband switch is designed following a procedure that incorporates LC-ladder low-pass filter theory, enabling the straightforward synthesis of a single-pole-multi-throw switch with a desired response. The implemented SP4T switch achieves isolation of > 35 dB and insertion loss of < 2 dB in the 4-K cryogenic measurements from dc to 20 GHz (the upper limit of our cryo-measurement facility). With a low power consumption of merely 0.6 μW, the proposed switch is suitable for various multiplexing and microwave measurement applications operating at cryogenic temperatures.

articleTitle: SiGe Transmitter and Receiver with Integrated Mixers and LO Chains for K/Ka Band Phased Array Systems
abstract: This paper presents a Ka-band transmitter and a K-band receiver RFICs for SatCom Phased-Array Systems. The circuits are fabricated by using 130-nm SiGe:C BiCMOS technology. They share the same architecture having 4-channels RF front end with integrated mixers and LO chain including the frequency multiplier. RX measurements results have shown 40 dB of gain, 2.7 dB of NF and 17 dB of image rejection with a total power consumption of 484 mW. TX RFIC achieves 25 dB of peak small signal gain and 8.5 dBm of OP1dB with a total power consumption of 690 mW. The area size, for both chips, amount to 12 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (pads included).

articleTitle: Characterization of Schottky Diodes at Wafer Level for Frequency Multipliers Applications Based on RF Coplanar Measurements
abstract: While Schottky diode for THz generation have been extensively studied over last decades, technological developments are still required to reach the physical limits of these devices, such as breakdown voltage or sub-μm devices, but also efficient thermal management in particular before their integration into waveguide packaging. We propose to investigate the DC/RF performances at device level without any integration/packaging encapsulation that require complex and time-consuming efforts. Thus, we report on initial characterization of on-wafer GaAs Schottky diodes, used as frequency doubler and pumped at 95 GHz.

articleTitle: High-Linearity and Low-Noise Tunable C/X-Band GaN Filters for Robust Highly Integrated Front-Ends
abstract: This paper presents two tunable recursive active filters fabricated in 250 nm and 150 nm GaN MMIC processes. The first filter is tunable at 9.8-10.7 GHz with a measured gain of 13-15 dB, NF=8.3-8.9 dB, 45 of rejection (Q≤70) and input third order intercept point (IIP3) of 10-11 dBm (the output power was measured up to an input power of 0.9 W). A 7.3-8.2 GHz tunable GaN filter has a measured gain of 9-12 dB, NF=3.9-4.2 dB, 42 dB of rejection (Q≤20) and IIP3=5-11 dBm. The two tunable GaN filters demonstrate a relatively high gain, linearity and rejection as well as comparatively low filter noise figure values at C/X-band.

articleTitle: 6-12.5 GHz, 0.0076 mm2, Low-Power PLL in 22 nm FDSOI for Multi Lane Applications
abstract: This work presents the design, implementation, and characterisation of a fully-integrated phase-locked loop in 22 nm FDSOI CMOS technology. The proposed PLL employs a feed-forward ring-based oscillator to achieve a compact footprint and wide tuning range. The proposed architecture is validated by designing a prototype that operates from 6 GHz to 12.5 GHz utilizing a 50 MHz reference. The power consumption at 12.5 GHz is 5.34 mW, and occupying only 0.0076 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> chip area. The measured phase noise at 12.5 GHz is -101.3 dBc/Hz, and the root-mean-square jitter is 306 fs. The achieved figure-of-merit is -288 dB.

articleTitle: Design and Experimental Characterization of an Asymmetric GaN MMIC Doherty Power Amplifier for Ka-Band Transmitters
abstract: This paper presents the design and experimental characterization of an asymmetric Ka-Band Doherty power amplifier based on a 0.12 µm GaN MMIC process. The design relies on the identification of an optimum load modulation trajectory on the load-pull contours of the main PA. The fabricated prototype shows a peak output power of 34 dBm and an 8-dB back-off power added efficiency of 17% at 28.3 GHz. When tested with a 100 MHz channel 5G signal, the amplifier demonstrates good intrinsic linearity and it is linearizable using digital predistortion.

articleTitle: A 0.5W <3dB IL DC-67GHz SPDT Switch in 16nm FinFET with Local Substrate Floating Technique
abstract: This paper presents a low-loss broadband SPDT T/R switch with <3dB insertion loss, >22dB isolation, and half-watt input 1dB compression point at 28GHz in TSMC 16nm FinFET process. By floating the local substrate in the vicinity of the switch device, loss and parasitic reduction can be achieved due to increased shunt impedance in the substrate network. It also helps provide more balanced voltage swing division within stacked transistors. Together with the introduced voltage swing on the deep-n-well to p-substrate diode, significant improvement in large-signal linearity is observed at mm-Wave. The measured prototype achieves DC to 67GHz operation with its performance at 28GHz as 1.86dB insertion loss, 29.4dB isolation, and 27.5dBm input 1dB compression point using only three stacked devices. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported mm-Wave SPDT switch using TSMC 16nm FinFET process.

articleTitle: G-Band Large-Signal Characterization of InP/GaAsSb DHBTs with Record 38% Power Added Efficiency at 170 GHz
abstract: We report the small- and large- signal performance of 250 nm InP/GaAsSb Double Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors (DHBTs) with an optimized epitaxial structure for high power and high efficiency applications in G-band. In class-A operation at 170 GHz, we show a saturated output power P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OUT,SAT</inf> = 10.7 dBm with a simultaneous record power-added efficiency PAE = 38.6%. Combined with the reported small-signal cut-off frequencies f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>/f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MAX</inf> > 0.5/1.1 THz, this makes InP/GaAsSb DHBTs very attractive for high-power and high-efficiency sub-mm-wave power amplifiers (PA).

articleTitle: Integrated high speed graphene photodetectors for sub-THz links in the D-Band
abstract: We report on ultrafast photonic integrated detectors with bandwidth exceeding 180 GHz. The device is fabricated using a CVD-grown large angle twisted-bilayer graphene as active material. We demonstrate the use of this device as a photonic-aided D-band upconverter operating at 140 GHz carrier frequency, performing 10Gb/s QPSK and 4Gb/s 16-QAM signals transmission.

articleTitle: A 434MHz Wakeup Receiver Analog Frontend based on a Switched Injection-Triggered Oscillator with -91 dBm Input Sensitivity and 175 pJ/bit Efficiency
abstract: A 434 MHz analog frontend for wakeup receivers based on a switched injection-triggered oscillator (SITO) designed in IHP SGB25V 250 nm BiCMOS technology is presented. On-off keying (OOK) demodulation is performed by evaluating the ramp-up time of a one-port oscillator. The oscillator drives a dual resonator consisting of an off-chip LC parallel tank in parallel to a surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator. In conjunction with an antenna switch the SAW resonator alternatingly accumulates signal energy and emits it as a pulse to trigger the oscillator ramp-up. This results in a high measured input sensitivity of -91dBm (without coding) while delivering a narrow measured 3dB input filtering bandwidth of 166kHz due to the high quality factor of the SAW resonator. Bitwise duty cycling leads to an energy efficient receiver frontend with a low measured DC energy per bit of 175pJ. Data rate and DC power can be scaled over a wide range from 100bps at 17.5nW up to 15kbps at 2.6μW (all measured).

articleTitle: High-Gain 664 GHz Low-Noise Amplifier Modules Based on Advanced InGaAs HEMT Technologies
abstract: Two compact WR-1.5 (500–750 GHz) low-noise amplifier (LNA) circuits have been developed, based on miniaturized thin-film microstrip lines (TFMSL) utilizing a 35 nm InGaAs-on-GaAs and a more advanced 20 nm InGaAs-on-Si high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) technology. The fabricated ten-stage InGaAs-on-GaAs LNA circuit achieved a maximum gain of 22 dB at 618 GHz and more than 19 dB in the frequency range from 602 to 672 GHz, while the InGaAs-on-Si S-MMIC demonstrates a small-signal gain of more than 20 dB between 582 and 656 GHz. For low-loss packaging of the circuits, waveguide-to-microstrip transitions (E-plane probes) have been monolithically integrated in the only 25 µm thick LNA MMICs. The realized InGaAs-on-GaAs LNA module achieved an average gain of 18 dB around 660 GHz and a room temperature (T = 293 K) noise figure of 12 dB in the frequency band of operation. The packaged InGaAs-on-Si LNA demonstrated a record gain of well above 20 dB around 620 GHz and an average noise figure of only 11 dB between 620 and 660 GHz.

articleTitle: Navigating Challenges in Doherty Power Amplifier Design for Millimeter-Wave Frequencies
abstract: The paper addresses some of the challenges associated with implementing multi-stage Doherty power amplifiers at millimeter waves. The routing of the bias lines is analyzed for several configurations, including two-way and three-way, highlighting how it can impact performance in the presence of significant crosstalk between the metal layers in integrated technologies. Additionally, the paper discusses and provides a quantitative estimate of the Doherty gain penalty with respect to corporate amplifier configurations, a factor that may hinder the adoption of this architecture at millimeter waves and that calls for a careful trade-off between intrinsic technology gain and number of driver stages.

articleTitle: Substrate Noise Mitigation Using a High Resistivity Substrate: The Case of a 14 GHz VCO on 28nm FD-SOI CMOS
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of silicon substrate resistivity on substrate noise coupling and how higher resistivity substrates improve the spectral purity of voltage-controlled oscillators (VCOs). Three VCOs were designed in the 28 nm fully depleted Silicon-on-Insulator (FD-SOI) technology and implemented on process-of-reference (POR) wafers (10 Ω.cm) as well as high-resistivity (HR) wafers (1 kΩ.cm). The output spectrum of the VCOs is measured with and without the injection of a 0 dBm noise signal into the substrate. Results show the highest reduction in the parasitic spurs caused by the noise signal to be more than 26 dBs when using a passivated HR substrate. To the best of the author’s knowledge, this is the first time VCOs are fabricated and measured on HR substrates in FD-SOI technology to explore their effectiveness in the reduction of substrate noise coupling.

articleTitle: Frequency-Domain Stability Analysis of Non-Linear Circuits driven by Random Modulated signals
abstract: A frequency-domain stability analysis of nonlinear circuits driven by a microwave Random-Modulated (RM) signal is presented. This stability analysis generalizes the already proposed method for CW generators to random modulated signals. The method is applied to perform the stability analysis of a designed and fabricated 20W/S-Band Quasi-MMIC GaN asymmetric Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA). The amplifier operates in the 3.2-3.6GHz bandwidth. It is driven by a generator modulated by a 16 QAM signal at 10MS/s. The simulated dynamic and stability results are all extracted from a frequency-domain simulation.

articleTitle: A Compensated Finite-Ground Elevated Coplanar Waveguide Interconnect Strategy for InP Based Integrated Circuits Above 100 GHz
abstract: In this paper, a low-loss interconnect strategy for InP integrated circuits operating above 100 GHz is proposed. The interconnect strategy is based upon finite-ground elevated coplanar waveguide (FG-ECPW) structures and requires no through-substrate vias (TSVs) or backside processing. To minimize the reflection losses at the FG-ECPW discontinuities, the ground bridge parasitics are compensated leading to a seamless transmission characteristic through FG-ECPW structures such as Tee-junctions, bends and crosses. The compensated FG-ECPW interconnects have been implemented in a high-speed, mixed-signal InP DHBT technology from III-V Lab. A compensated FG-ECPW meandered line with an accumulated length of 1.65 mm shows a resonance free, single-mode transmission characteristic with an average insertion loss of 2.4 dB in the full D-band from 110-170 GHz. The measured improvement in insertion loss is 3.7 dB at 170 GHz over a similar noncompensated FG-ECPW meandered line.

articleTitle: Low-Power Dual-Core Inductively Coupled 40 GHz Push-Push VCO in 22nm FDSOI CMOS
abstract: We present a 39.6-to-41.8 GHz push-push dual-core cross-coupled voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) in a 22 nm FDSOI CMOS technology. The two cores are coupled inductively. The passive core coupling device serves multiple purposes: a) as H2 filter to enhance phase noise; b) to provide bias; and c) to extract the second harmonic in a non-invasive way and forward it to the output buffer. The VCO achieves in measurement a low phase noise of −102 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset at 39.65 GHz and an output power of − 10 dBm. The VCO including buffers dissipates 24.5 mW from a single 0.75 V supply, while both cores consume only 19.7 mW. Fundamental rejection of better 37 dB is achieved over the entire frequency tuning range (FTR). The chip occupies only 0.3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including pads. The circuit achieves a very good FoM of −181 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset.

articleTitle: A Frequency-Agile Digital-to-RF Power Amplifier in 22 nm FD-SOI CMOS Technology
abstract: This work presents a frequency-agile digital-to-RF power amplifier (DPA) in 22 nm FD-SOI CMOS technology that supports carrier frequencies from 2 GHz to 6 GHz. The DPA is based on a current-mode, switched-mode power amplifier (CM-SMPA) that combines conductance modulation and radio frequency pulse-width modulation (RFPWM). Compared to a CM-SMPA with conductance modulation only, the number of required unit cells and thus the wiring effort can be reduced and the back-off efficiency of the DPA can be increased. The peak output power is 22.5 dBm with a peak drain efficiency and a system efficiency of 35.7 % and 33.1 %, respectively. For a 40 MBd 64-QAM signal at a carrier frequency of 3.6 GHz, an EVM of -30.9 dB is achieved. Compared to other sub-6 GHz DPAs, it provides the highest carrier frequency range with the highest demonstrated signal bandwidth of 1 GHz.

articleTitle: A new 45nm RFSOI Technology Optimized for Low Power, High Performance mmWave Applications
abstract: In this paper we introduce a new 45nm technology with a focus on mmWave 5G FEM. The technology features a high resistivity substrate with dual thick Cu for low loss BEOL passives, RVT NFET with fT/fmax ~300/420 GHz and NFmin <0.9 dB at 28 GHz, power amplifier FETs with ft/fmax/Vmax ~150 GHz/350 GHz/1.8X and Switch FET with Ron.Coff ~86 fs. High performance power amplifier (PA), low noise amplifier (LNA) and switch reference circuits are demmostrated. The technology also provides low leakage std cell, I/O and efuse IP.

articleTitle: Wideband fully integrated GaN Doherty Power Amplifier Module for 5G massive MIMO applications
abstract: This paper presents the design and performances of a power amplifier module (PAM) in 50V GaN technology for C-Band massive-MIMO 5G applications. Thanks to the 2-way inverted E-Doherty architecture, this device presents wide band performances allowing good linearizability for wideband instantaneous bandwidth applications without compromising the efficiency. This 2-stages amplifier delivers an output power (P5dB) higher than 47.5dBm and a linear gain of 30dB. At 39dBm average output power (Pav), with an instantaneous Bandwidth (iBW) of 400MHz, the ACLR after DPD reaches - 50.1dBc and 46.7% linearized total drain efficiency. On dual band application with iBW of 530MHz a linearized ACLR of - 52.3dBc is reached with a total drain efficiency of 45.4%.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Integrated GaN Diodes as Varactors for Tunable MMIC PAs from C- to K-Band
abstract: Variable capacitors (varactors) can act as powerful enablers for reconfigurable RF power amplifiers (PAs) in microwave monolithic integrated circuit (MMIC) technology. While their use for custom impedance tuning has been widely explored for sub-6 GHz frequencies, an experimental work is here performed to address the prospective use of RF power Schottky diodes as varactors for MMIC PAs operating from C to K band. Small- and large-signal measurements of diodes with different layouts are reported for two modern Gallium Nitride (GaN) High-Electron-Mobility Transistor (HEMT) process technologies. Capacitance and quality factor (Q-factor) of the varactors have been extracted, obtaining a measured tuning range in the frequency bands of interest of about 20% to 40% for the two technologies. The measured Q-factors, while decreasing with frequency, result to be up to 100 in the lower frequency bands, while being comparable to an equivalent integrated capacitor in the higher frequency bands.

articleTitle: A 14-GHz LC-VCO with SiGe Anti-Parallel Core Configuration and a High-Quality Inductor
abstract: In this paper, A 14-GHz LC Voltage-Controlled Oscillator (VCO) is introduced employing a Silicon-Germanium (SiGe) Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor (HBT) anti-parallel core. The design introduces a high quality factor inductor alongside a 3-bit binary-weighted capacitor bank, which utilizes SiGe anti-parallel switches. This setup integrates a secondary LC-VCO in an anti-parallel arrangement with the primary core, further enhanced by a inverse-active SiGe HBT current mirror applied to both cores. The developed VCO achieves a Frequency Tuning Range (FTR) of 11.6%, covering frequencies from 13.26 to 14.9 GHz, and records a low phase noise (PN) of -116.2 dBc/Hz at a 1 MHz offset from 14 GHz, demonstrating 5.6 dB enhancement compared to the single-core VCO, with low 1/f<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> corner frequency of 150 kHz.

articleTitle: A Signal Source in J-Band with 237-287 GHz Tuning Range in a 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS Process
abstract: This article presents a J-band signal source fabricated in a 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS process which consists of a K-band voltage controlled oscillator (VCO), a D-band frequency quadrupler (X4) and an amplifier (AMP) and a J-band frequency doubler (X2). It has a tuning range of 19.1 % (237-287 GHz) centered at 262 GHz with an average output power of −3.1 dBm. Average measured phase noise is −78.4 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset. The chip has an area of 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and it consumes a maximum power of 622 mW. Thus it results in 0.15 % DC-to-RF efficiency. It stands out as a fully integrated state-of-the-art silicon-based signal source at J-band frequencies, with a wide tuning range and practical output power.
